| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Authentication.user) as user values(Authentication.src) as src from datamodel=Authentication where Authentication.app="globalprotect" Authentication.action="success" Authentication.endpoint_os_version="Microsoft Windows 10 Pro 64-bit" (Authentication.user_domain="" OR Authentication.user_domain="-" OR NOT Authentication.user_domain="*") by Authentication.user Authentication.src Authentication.endpoint_os_version | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email

          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")

New Threat Cluster OP-512 Targets Microsoft IIS Servers with Custom Web Shell Framework

The Hacker News
2026-06-05 11 use cases 5 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Cybersecurity researchers have discovered a previously unreported threat cluster dubbed OP-512 (where "OP" stands for "opponent") that has been observed&nbsp;targeting Microsoft Internet Information Services (IIS) servers to deploy a bespoke web shell framework. ReliaQuest has assessed with moderate to high confidence that the espionage-focused activity is linked to China. "OP-512 was highly

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] OP-512 Potato Suite SYSTEM escalation from IIS worker (SeImpersonate token abuse) · Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — New Threat Cluster OP-512 Targets Microsoft IIS Servers with Custom Web Shell Fr
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] IIS worker w3wp.exe writes .aspx/.ashx handler to upload/temp directory (OP-512 web shell drop)
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] OP-512 C2 beacon to ashx.lhlsjcb[.]com from IIS host · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] IIS w3wp.exe spawns whoami /priv or cmd.exe — OP-512 web shell command execution · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
OP-512 C2 beacon to ashx.lhlsjcb[.]com from IIS host AICommand & Control High
Detects DNS resolutions or HTTP egress to the OP-512 attacker-controlled domain ashx.lhlsjcb[.]com observed in the ReliaQuest report. Article-specific because this domain appeared ~75 days before the main intrusion as the initial staging beacon and is reused by the web shell's self-reporting fallback over DNS/HTTP. Rationale: The domain ashx.lhlsjcb[.]com is the only network IOC named in the ReliaQuest write-up; matching it across DNS and HTTP egress is a definitive OP-512 signal. Cross-checked the IOC pattern via the article's lead and MITRE T1071.004 mapping. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/004/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/001/
ATT&CKT1071.004 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security tooling (EDR, threat-intel proxy) sandbox-resolving the domain after an analyst lookup
  • DNS sinkhole infrastructure resolving the domain to a blackhole IP for blocking
  • SIEM enrichment lookups for the IOC itself generating outbound DNS
  • Legitimate hosts on the same parent domain (none expected — lhlsjcb.com is single-purpose)
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe", "SenseIR.exe", "MsMpEng.exe", "smartscreen.exe")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: Confirm the resolving host is an IIS server or in scope; identify the initiating process (w3wp.exe is the smoking gun) and look for any preceding inbound HTTP POST to upload/temp directories. Step 2 — Contain: Sinkhole lhlsjcb.com at the DNS layer, isolate the host from the network, snapshot the IIS web roots and inetpub directories before reboot. Step 3 — Hunt: Pivot the host for w3wp.exe → cmd/whoami/Potato child processes, newly-created .aspx/.ashx files with anomalous timestomped MFT entries, and any other hosts that resolved lhlsjcb.com in the last 120 days.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(90d)
| where RemoteUrl has "lhlsjcb.com" or RemoteUrl has_cs "ashx.lhlsjcb.com"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort, Protocol
| order by Timestamp asc
let ioc_domain = "lhlsjcb.com";
(union isfuzzy=true
    (DnsEvents
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
        | where Name has ioc_domain
        | project TimeGenerated, Host = Computer, ClientIP, Domain = Name, QueryTypeName, Source = "DnsEvents"),
    (ImDnsActivity
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
        | where DnsQuery has ioc_domain
        | project TimeGenerated, Host = DvcHostname, ClientIP = SrcIpAddr, Domain = DnsQuery, QueryTypeName = DnsQueryTypeName, Source = "ImDnsActivity"),
    (CommonSecurityLog
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
        | where RequestURL has ioc_domain or DestinationHostName has ioc_domain or DestinationDnsDomain has ioc_domain
        | project TimeGenerated, Host = SourceHostName, ClientIP = SourceIP, Domain = coalesce(DestinationHostName, DestinationDnsDomain), URL = RequestURL, Source = "CommonSecurityLog")
)
| order by TimeGenerated asc
title: OP-512 C2 Domain ashx.lhlsjcb.com
id: 6c14a2f9-9b1d-4d8f-9c70-1a3a92b1f3ce
description: Detects DNS or HTTP egress to the OP-512 attacker-controlled domain lhlsjcb.com reported by ReliaQuest as the staging/self-reporting C2 for the IIS web shell framework.
references:
    - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/new-threat-cluster-op-512-targets.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/05
tags:
    - attack.t1071.004
    - attack.t1071.001
logsource:
    category: dns
status: experimental
detection:
    selection:
        QueryName|contains: 'lhlsjcb.com'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - None expected; domain is attacker-controlled
level: high
(source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.defender OR linux.syslog) AND (@QueryName:*lhlsjcb.com* OR @DnsQuery:*lhlsjcb.com* OR @DestinationHostname:*lhlsjcb.com* OR @network.destination.domain:*lhlsjcb.com*))
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest
| regex("lhlsjcb\\.com", field=DomainName)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName], function=[count(), min(@timestamp), max(@timestamp)])
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(DNS.src) as src values(DNS.query) as query from datamodel=Network_Resolution where DNS.query="*lhlsjcb.com" OR DNS.query="ashx.lhlsjcb.com" by host | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)` | append [| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Web.src) as src values(Web.url) as url from datamodel=Web where Web.url="*lhlsjcb.com*" by host | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`] | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(DNS.src) as src values(DNS.query) as query from datamodel=Network_Resolution where DNS.query="*lhlsjcb.com" OR DNS.query="ashx.lhlsjcb.com" by host | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)` | append [| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Web.src) as src values(Web.url) as url from datamodel=Web where Web.url="*lhlsjcb.com*" by host | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`] | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
IIS worker w3wp.exe writes .aspx/.ashx handler to upload/temp directory (OP-512 web shell drop) AIInstallation High
Detects the IIS worker process w3wp.exe writing ASP.NET handler files (.aspx, .ashx, .asmx) into upload or temp directories — the exact drop pattern ReliaQuest observed for the OP-512 three-shell framework. Combines parent-process (w3wp.exe) and target-extension predicates to keep false positives down on legitimate deployment activity. Rationale: ReliaQuest explicitly names w3wp.exe as the process that dropped the web shell into the application's upload directory. The parent (w3wp.exe) + extension (.aspx/.ashx) + path (upload/temp) triple gives strong specificity to OP-512 vs legitimate publish flows. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1505/003/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate web application's upload feature accepting an .aspx file from an admin user (rare; most apps block this MIME)
  • Visual Studio publish / Web Deploy through the worker process during app deployment
  • SharePoint or DotNetNuke template extraction writing handler files to /temp
  • Vendor patch script extracting .ashx fragments into App_Data
  • Custom-built CMS legitimately writing .aspx pages at runtime (e.g. Sitecore, Umbraco)
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !in~ ("system") or RequestSourceIP !startswith "10."
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: Pull the file's hash, verify it isn't on a known-good IIS image baseline, and check the IIS access log for the inbound POST/PUT request immediately preceding the write (note the source IP, User-Agent, and target URL). Step 2 — Contain: Quarantine the file (rename to .bak in place to preserve forensic timestamps), suspend the application pool, and block the source IP at the perimeter. Step 3 — Hunt: Search for two additional uniquely-generated shells in the same web root (OP-512 plants three), check for w3wp.exe → DNS queries to lhlsjcb.com, and look for w3wp.exe child processes (cmd, whoami, Potato variants) in the next 24h.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "w3wp.exe"
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated", "FileModified", "FileRenamed")
| where FileName endswith ".aspx" or FileName endswith ".ashx" or FileName endswith ".asmx" or FileName endswith ".asax"
| where FolderPath has_any ("\\upload", "\\uploads", "\\temp", "\\tmp", "\\App_Data", "\\images", "\\files")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RequestSourceIP
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has "w3wp.exe"
| where EventType in ("FileCreated", "FileModified", "FileRenamed")
| where TargetFileExtension in~ ("aspx", "ashx", "asmx", "asax")
   or TargetFileName endswith ".aspx"
   or TargetFileName endswith ".ashx"
   or TargetFileName endswith ".asmx"
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("\\upload", "\\uploads", "\\temp", "\\tmp", "\\App_Data", "\\images", "\\files")
| project TimeGenerated, Host = DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: IIS w3wp.exe Writes ASP.NET Handler to Upload or Temp Directory
id: 8a2e5d11-7b40-4c5b-9f8a-3d5b6e0c8e21
description: Detects the IIS worker process w3wp.exe creating ASP.NET handler files (.aspx/.ashx/.asmx/.asax) in upload, temp, or App_Data directories — the OP-512 web shell drop pattern.
references:
    - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/new-threat-cluster-op-512-targets.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/05
tags:
    - attack.t1505.003
    - attack.t1190
logsource:
    category: file_event
    product: windows
status: experimental
detection:
    selection_proc:
        Image|endswith: '\w3wp.exe'
    selection_ext:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '.aspx'
            - '.ashx'
            - '.asmx'
            - '.asax'
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\upload'
            - '\uploads'
            - '\temp'
            - '\tmp'
            - '\App_Data'
            - '\images'
            - '\files'
    condition: selection_proc and selection_ext and selection_path
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate ASP.NET application publishing via web-deploy through the worker process (rare)
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @Image:(*\w3wp.exe OR *\W3WP.EXE OR *\W3wp.exe) @TargetFilename:(*.aspx OR *.ashx OR *.asmx OR *.asax OR *.ASPX OR *.ASHX) @TargetFilename:(*\upload* OR *\Upload* OR *\UPLOAD* OR *\temp* OR *\Temp* OR *\TEMP* OR *\App_Data* OR *\images* OR *\files*)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| ContextImageFileName=/\\w3wp\.exe$/i
| TargetFileName=/\.(aspx|ashx|asmx|asax)$/i
| regex("\\\\(upload[s]?|temp|tmp|App_Data|images|files)\\\\", field=TargetFileName, flags="i")
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName], function=[count(), min(@timestamp)])
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as file_path values(Filesystem.process_name) as process_name from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.process_name="w3wp.exe" (Filesystem.file_name="*.aspx" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.ashx" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.asmx" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.asax") (Filesystem.file_path="*\\upload*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\uploads*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\temp*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\tmp*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\App_Data*") by host Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as file_path values(Filesystem.process_name) as process_name from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.process_name="w3wp.exe" (Filesystem.file_name="*.aspx" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.ashx" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.asmx" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.asax") (Filesystem.file_path="*\\upload*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\uploads*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\temp*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\tmp*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\App_Data*") by host Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
IIS w3wp.exe spawns whoami /priv or cmd.exe — OP-512 web shell command execution AIActions on Objectives High
Detects the IIS worker w3wp.exe spawning interpreter or reconnaissance binaries (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, whoami.exe, net.exe) — directly matching ReliaQuest's observed OP-512 post-exploitation step of running whoami /priv from the web shell to confirm SYSTEM-level privileges after Potato Suite escalation. Rationale: ReliaQuest directly cites whoami /priv as the post-Potato verification command from OP-512, and the entire chain hinges on w3wp.exe being the parent. Parent (w3wp.exe) + child (recon binaries) is exactly the article's described observed sequence. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1505/003/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1033/
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1059.003 T1033 T1087
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Web admin diagnostics page running ipconfig/tasklist through a controlled API endpoint
  • Application Insights or APM agent shelling out to systeminfo on first run
  • Vendor IIS management plugin (Plesk, IIS Manager extensions) invoking sc.exe / net.exe
  • ASP.NET unhandled-exception handler calling cmd.exe to write a crash report (rare/poor practice but seen in legacy apps)
  • Internal vulnerability scanner authenticated probe of web app health endpoints
Suppression filter
| where not (FileName =~ "net.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("localgroup IIS_IUSRS", "start w3svc", "stop w3svc"))
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: Open the process tree — confirm w3wp.exe → cmd/whoami sequence and capture the full command-line; correlate to the preceding HTTP request in IIS logs (look for the URI of the dropped .aspx/.ashx shell). Step 2 — Contain: Stop the IIS application pool serving the implicated site, isolate the host, and snapshot memory if possible (Potato/SeImpersonate token will be evidential). Step 3 — Hunt: Pivot for any w3wp.exe child whose ProcessTokenElevation is SeImpersonatePrivilege or whose integrity level jumped to System (Potato Suite signature); review the last 90 days for other w3wp.exe → cmd sequences across all internet-facing IIS hosts.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "w3wp.exe"
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "whoami.exe", "net.exe", "net1.exe", "systeminfo.exe", "ipconfig.exe", "tasklist.exe", "hostname.exe", "wmic.exe", "reg.exe", "sc.exe")
| extend IsWhoamiPriv = (FileName =~ "whoami.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/priv", "/all", "/groups"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, IsWhoamiPriv
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\w3wp.exe"
| extend ChildName = tostring(split(NewProcessName, "\\")[-1])
| where ChildName in~ ("cmd.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "whoami.exe", "net.exe", "net1.exe", "systeminfo.exe", "ipconfig.exe", "tasklist.exe", "hostname.exe", "wmic.exe", "reg.exe", "sc.exe")
| extend IsWhoamiPriv = (ChildName =~ "whoami.exe" and CommandLine has_any ("/priv", "/all", "/groups"))
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, TokenElevationType, IsWhoamiPriv
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: IIS Worker w3wp.exe Spawns Recon Binary (OP-512)
id: 4f7b3c6a-2d11-4f8d-8a51-7e2b1a4c9e3f
description: Detects w3wp.exe spawning cmd/powershell/whoami/net/systeminfo as a child, consistent with OP-512 web shell post-exploitation reconnaissance after Potato Suite SYSTEM escalation.
references:
    - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/new-threat-cluster-op-512-targets.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/05
tags:
    - attack.t1505.003
    - attack.t1059.003
    - attack.t1033
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
status: experimental
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith: '\w3wp.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\whoami.exe'
            - '\net.exe'
            - '\net1.exe'
            - '\systeminfo.exe'
            - '\ipconfig.exe'
            - '\tasklist.exe'
            - '\hostname.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\reg.exe'
            - '\sc.exe'
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child
falsepositives:
    - IIS web apps that legitimately shell out to net.exe / ipconfig.exe for diagnostics endpoints (rare)
level: high
source:(windows.security OR windows.sysmon) (@EventID:4688 OR @EventID:1) @ParentImage:(*\w3wp.exe OR *\W3WP.EXE) @Image:(*\cmd.exe OR *\CMD.EXE OR *\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\pwsh.exe OR *\whoami.exe OR *\WHOAMI.EXE OR *\net.exe OR *\net1.exe OR *\systeminfo.exe OR *\ipconfig.exe OR *\tasklist.exe OR *\hostname.exe OR *\wmic.exe OR *\reg.exe OR *\sc.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/^w3wp\.exe$/i
| ImageFileName=/\\(cmd|powershell|pwsh|whoami|net1?|systeminfo|ipconfig|tasklist|hostname|wmic|reg|sc)\.exe$/i
| WhoamiPriv := if(ImageFileName=/whoami\.exe$/i AND CommandLine=/\/(priv|all|groups)/i, "true", "false")
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=[count(), min(@timestamp)])

OP-512 Potato Suite SYSTEM escalation from IIS worker (SeImpersonate token abuse) AIExploitation High
Detects token-impersonation privilege escalation from the IIS app-pool identity to NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM — the exact Potato Suite (RottenPotato/JuicyPotato/GodPotato/RoguePotato) chain ReliaQuest observed after OP-512 dropped its web shells. Pivots on child of w3wp.exe with integrity-level jump to System, plus Windows 4672 'special privileges' assignments to non-service accounts. Rationale: ReliaQuest explicitly names the Potato Suite as OP-512's escalation tool from the IIS app-pool to SYSTEM. The IIS-worker-as-parent plus Potato binary-name keywords plus integrity-level jump make this a high-fidelity escalation indicator. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1134/001/ • https://github.com/ohpe/juicy-potato • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1068/
ATT&CKT1134.001 T1068
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Pentester engagement running Potato-family tools on internal IIS servers
  • Renaming the binary (real attackers do; tune on behaviour rather than name where possible)
  • Legitimate SeImpersonatePrivilege use by SQL Server / Exchange service accounts running on the same host
  • IIS application pool configured to run as LocalSystem (no escalation needed; legacy misconfig)
  • Custom IIS module that legitimately impersonates the calling user token
Suppression filter
| where AccountName !in~ ("defaultapppool", "iisapppooluser") or InitiatingProcessAccountName != AccountName
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: Confirm parent w3wp.exe → child elevated process, capture the binary hash and command line, and review the recent w3wp.exe file-write events for the originating web shell drop. Step 2 — Contain: Kill the elevated process, isolate the host, dump memory if forensic capacity exists, and rotate any local-account / service-account passwords that may have been touched once SYSTEM was held. Step 3 — Hunt: Pivot for any process spawned with `SeImpersonatePrivilege` from a non-service caller across the fleet, hunt for COM-coercion event sequences (RPC EVENT 5145 to MS-DCOM endpoints), and review all internet-facing IIS hosts for the OP-512 three-shell drop signature.
let PotatoFingerprints = dynamic(["juicypotato", "rottenpotato", "sweetpotato", "godpotato", "roguepotato", "localpotato", "remotepotato", "printspoofer", "efspotato"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "w3wp.exe"
| where ProcessIntegrityLevel in~ ("System", "High")
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any (PotatoFingerprints)
   or FileName has_any (PotatoFingerprints)
   or InitiatingProcessTokenElevation =~ "TokenElevationTypeFull" and AccountName =~ "SYSTEM" and InitiatingProcessAccountName !in~ ("system", "network service", "local service")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, DeviceId, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, ProcessIntegrityLevel, ProcessTokenElevation, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessIntegrityLevel
| order by Timestamp desc
let PotatoNames = dynamic(["juicypotato", "rottenpotato", "sweetpotato", "godpotato", "roguepotato", "localpotato", "remotepotato", "printspoofer", "efspotato"]);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\w3wp.exe"
| extend ChildName = tolower(tostring(split(NewProcessName, "\\")[-1]))
| where TokenElevationType in ("%%1936", "%%1937")  // Full or Default-elevated
   or CommandLine has_any (PotatoNames)
   or ChildName has_any (PotatoNames)
   or (SubjectUserSid == "S-1-5-18" and ParentProcessName endswith "\\w3wp.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, SubjectUserSid, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, TokenElevationType
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Potato Suite Privilege Escalation from IIS w3wp.exe
id: 9e3c12b8-1d6a-44e9-bf7c-2c0a3b8e15dc
description: Detects Potato-family (Juicy/Rotten/Sweet/God/Rogue/Local/Remote/PrintSpoofer/EFS) privilege escalation invoked from the IIS worker w3wp.exe, matching OP-512's observed SYSTEM escalation.
references:
    - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/new-threat-cluster-op-512-targets.html
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1134/001/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/05
tags:
    - attack.t1134.001
    - attack.t1068
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
status: experimental
detection:
    parent_iis:
        ParentImage|endswith: '\w3wp.exe'
    potato_keywords:
        - CommandLine|contains:
            - 'juicypotato'
            - 'rottenpotato'
            - 'sweetpotato'
            - 'godpotato'
            - 'roguepotato'

level: critical
source:(windows.security OR windows.sysmon) (@EventID:4688 OR @EventID:1) @ParentImage:(*\w3wp.exe OR *\W3WP.EXE) (@CommandLine:(*juicypotato* OR *JuicyPotato* OR *rottenpotato* OR *RottenPotato* OR *sweetpotato* OR *SweetPotato* OR *godpotato* OR *GodPotato* OR *roguepotato* OR *RoguePotato* OR *printspoofer* OR *PrintSpoofer* OR *efspotato* OR *EfsPotato*) OR @Image:(*potato* OR *Potato* OR *POTATO* OR *printspoofer* OR *PrintSpoofer*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/^w3wp\.exe$/i
| (regex("(?i)(juicypotato|rottenpotato|sweetpotato|godpotato|roguepotato|localpotato|remotepotato|printspoofer|efspotato)", field=CommandLine)
   OR regex("(?i)(potato|printspoofer)", field=ImageFileName)
   OR IntegrityLevel="System")
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, IntegrityLevel], function=[count(), min(@timestamp)])
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process values(Processes.process_integrity_level) as integrity from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name="w3wp.exe" OR Processes.parent_process_path="*\\inetsrv\\w3wp.exe") (Processes.process_integrity_level="System" OR Processes.process_integrity_level="high") by host Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where user!="SYSTEM" OR process_name!="w3wp.exe" | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process values(Processes.process_integrity_level) as integrity from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name="w3wp.exe" OR Processes.parent_process_path="*\\inetsrv\\w3wp.exe") (Processes.process_integrity_level="System" OR Processes.process_integrity_level="high") by host Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where user!="SYSTEM" OR process_name!="w3wp.exe" | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`

    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time

         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject

| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]

Hackers Exploit Critical Everest Forms Pro WordPress Plugin Flaw to Take Over Sites

The Hacker News
2026-06-05 14 use cases 7 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Threat actors are actively exploiting a critical security flaw in Everest Forms Pro, a WordPress plugin with about 4,000 active installations, to execute arbitrary code, leading to a complete site compromise. The vulnerability in question is CVE-2026-3300 (CVSS score: 9.8), a remote code execution bug impacting all versions of the plugin up to, and including, 1.9.12. A patch for the flaw was

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Everest Forms Pro RCE exploit attempt from named source IPs · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Everest Forms Pro Calculation Addon PHP injection payload in form submission · Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Hackers Exploit Critical Everest Forms Pro WordPress Plugin Flaw to Take Over Si
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] WordPress rogue 'diksimarina' admin account creation request · [LLM] WordPress PHP worker spawning shell or download utility post-RCE
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
Everest Forms Pro RCE exploit attempt from named source IPs AIDelivery Medium
Hunts inbound HTTP requests to vulnerable WordPress sites from the four IPv4 sources Wordfence attributed to the CVE-2026-3300 exploitation campaign. Highest fidelity signal since the IPs were named in the original advisory and have driven 29,300+ blocked attempts since 2026-04-13. Rationale: Wordfence's named source IPs are the highest-confidence pivot in the article. Combining IP source + WordPress admin-ajax/everest_forms URI keeps the false-positive surface near zero. Cross-checked with Wordfence's advisory and abuse.ch ThreatFox for IP reputation. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wordfence.com/blog/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/
ATT&CKT1190 T1659
Data sourcesWeb.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate security researchers / vulnerability scanners using shared VPS infrastructure that happens to overlap with attacker IP blocks
  • Internal red-team exercises probing WordPress installs from approved testing IPs
  • Cloudflare/CDN re-presenting client IPs causing IP attribution confusion
  • Honeypot research traffic from threat-intel firms scanning for the same CVE
Suppression filter
| where csUserAgent !has_any ("WPScan","Nessus","Qualys","InternalRedTeam")
Response runbook
1. Triage: confirm the destination is a WordPress site running Everest Forms Pro; pull the full HTTP request body from WAF/proxy logs to see if a PHP injection payload was attempted; check Everest Forms plugin version (vulnerable <=1.9.12). 2. Contain: block the four source IPs at perimeter and WAF; if the plugin version is unpatched, take the site behind maintenance mode and update to 1.9.13+; rotate WordPress salts in wp-config.php. 3. Hunt: review wp_users for new admin accounts (especially 'diksimarina' or any account created in the past 60 days); diff wp-content/uploads, wp-content/plugins/, wp-content/themes/ for new .php files; review outbound traffic from the web tier for command-and-control.

| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in ("202.56.2.126","209.146.60.26","15.235.166.18","185.78.165.153")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("w3wp.exe","httpd.exe","nginx.exe","php-cgi.exe","php-fpm.exe")
   or RemotePort in (80, 443, 8080, 8443)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, LocalPort, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ActionType
| order by Timestamp desc

| where csUriStem has_any ("admin-ajax.php","everest_forms","wp-json")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, cIP, csMethod, csUriStem, csUriQuery, csUserAgent, scStatus),
(CommonSecurityLog

| where SourceIP in ("202.56.2.126","209.146.60.26","15.235.166.18","185.78.165.153")

Everest Forms Pro Calculation Addon PHP injection payload in form submission AIExploitation Medium
Hunts POST bodies to WordPress endpoints containing PHP code-context characters that escape sanitize_text_field() and reach eval() in process_filter(). Targets the specific injection shape described by Wordfence — single quotes followed by PHP functions like system, exec, base64_decode, or backticks. Rationale: Wordfence quotes the bug as 'concatenating user-submitted form field values into a PHP code string without proper escaping before passing it to eval()' — the discriminating signal is PHP-function tokens (system, exec, base64_decode, shell_exec, assert) plus single-quote-break characters in a POST to admin-ajax/everest_forms. Cross-checked the wp-json everest path against the Everest Forms plugin source. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wordfence.com/blog/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate plugin functionality where form descriptions or labels contain words like 'system' or 'exec' as literal text
  • Security plugins (WordFence, Sucuri) logging blocked PHP injection attempts into the same URI parameters
  • Form builders allowing PHP-syntax-like custom fields in calculation expressions
  • Internal pen-test traffic running CVE-2026-3300 PoC payloads
Suppression filter
| where not(csUserAgent has_any ("WPScan","Burp","Nessus")) and not(csUriQuery has "_wpnonce" and csUriQuery has "action=heartbeat")
Response runbook
1. Triage: extract the raw POST body from WAF/reverse-proxy logs and inspect the calculated-field values for PHP token chains; confirm the destination WordPress site has Everest Forms Pro <=1.9.12 with the Calculation Addon enabled. 2. Contain: block the source IP at WAF, then upgrade Everest Forms Pro to 1.9.13+; if upgrade blocked, disable the Calculation Addon as a temporary mitigation. 3. Hunt: pivot on the source IP to find earlier reconnaissance traffic; check PHP error_log and access logs for the same form_id around the request time; review wp-content/uploads/ for new .php files and the wp_users table for newly-added admin accounts.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("w3wp.exe","httpd.exe","nginx.exe","php-fpm.exe")
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("admin-ajax.php","everest_forms")
| where AdditionalFields has_any ("system(","exec(","passthru(","base64_decode","shell_exec","assert(","'.system")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, AdditionalFields
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where csMethod == "POST"
| where csUriStem has_any ("admin-ajax.php","everest_forms","wp-json")
| where csUriQuery has_any ("system(","exec(","passthru(","base64_decode","shell_exec","assert(","%27.system","%27%2Bsystem","`","%60")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, cIP, csMethod, csUriStem, csUriQuery, csUserAgent, scStatus),

   or RequestCookies has_any ("system(","base64_decode")

WordPress rogue 'diksimarina' admin account creation request AIInstallation High
Hunts the specific payload Wordfence saw most commonly in CVE-2026-3300 exploitation: creation of a WordPress administrator account named 'diksimarina' with email 'diksimarina@gmail.com'. Hardcoded IOCs from the original advisory. Rationale: 'diksimarina' and 'diksimarina@gmail.com' are verbatim IOCs from Wordfence's report cited in the article — extremely high-fidelity strings unlikely to appear organically in benign traffic. Searching across multiple log surfaces (WAF, IIS, App Service, syslog) catches the payload regardless of where it lands. Cross-checked against: • https://www.wordfence.com/blog/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1136/001/
ATT&CKT1136.001 T1078.003
Data sourcesWeb.Web Change.Account_Management
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat intel feed ingestion: SOAR/SIEM pipelines processing the same IOC list and logging the string
  • Security researchers documenting/blogging the CVE locally with the IOC in URLs
  • Internal IR runbook traffic exercising the same string for tabletop drills
  • WAF block log entries quoting the matched payload (treat as actual block, not benign)
Suppression filter
| where not(csUriQuery has "action=heartbeat") and not(DeviceVendor has "SIEM" and SourceIP in ("<your-soar-ip>"))
Response runbook
1. Triage: query WordPress wp_users and wp_usermeta for any account named 'diksimarina' or email 'diksimarina@gmail.com'; check if the request returned 200/302; pull session IDs/cookies issued after the hit. 2. Contain: if the account exists, immediately remove it from wp_users + wp_usermeta and invalidate all WordPress sessions (rotate AUTH_KEY/SECURE_AUTH_KEY in wp-config.php); upgrade Everest Forms Pro to 1.9.13+; force-reset all other WP admin passwords. 3. Hunt: search for newly-written .php files under wp-content/{uploads,plugins,themes} in the 7-day window post-IOC; check outbound network for connections from the web tier to non-standard destinations; review scheduled wp-cron jobs and the wp_options table for malicious entries.
union
(DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(60d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("w3wp.exe","httpd.exe","nginx.exe","php-fpm.exe","php-cgi.exe")
| where AdditionalFields has_any ("diksimarina","diksimarina@gmail.com")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, InitiatingProcessFileName, AdditionalFields),
(DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(60d)
| where FolderPath has_any ("wp-content","wp-admin","wp-includes")
| where FileName endswith ".php"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("w3wp.exe","httpd.exe","nginx.exe","php-fpm.exe","php-cgi.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
| where csMethod == "POST"
| where csUriStem has_any ("admin-ajax.php","everest_forms","wp-json","wp-login.php","user-new.php")
| where csUriQuery has_any ("diksimarina","diksimarina%40gmail.com","diksimarina@gmail.com")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, cIP, csMethod, csUriStem, csUriQuery, csUserAgent, scStatus),
(CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
| where RequestURL has_any ("admin-ajax.php","everest_forms","wp-json")
   or DeviceProduct has "WAF"
| where Message has_any ("diksimarina","diksimarina@gmail.com")
   or RequestURL has "diksimarina"
   or RequestCookies has "diksimarina"
   or DeviceCustomString1 has "diksimarina"
   or DeviceCustomString2 has "diksimarina"
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, SourceIP, RequestMethod, RequestURL, Message, DeviceAction),
(AppServiceHTTPLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
| where CsUriQuery has_any ("diksimarina","diksimarina%40gmail.com")
   or CsUriStem has "diksimarina"
| project TimeGenerated, CsHost, CIp, CsMethod, CsUriStem, CsUriQuery, UserAgent, ScStatus),
(Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("diksimarina","diksimarina@gmail.com")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostIP, ProcessName, SyslogMessage)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

WordPress PHP worker spawning shell or download utility post-RCE AIInstallation Medium
Hunts the post-exploit behaviour where the PHP/Apache/Nginx worker process spawns sh, bash, wget, curl, python, perl, or nc — the natural follow-on after process_filter() eval() succeeds and the attacker drops a webshell or pulls a second-stage payload. Rationale: The article's kill-chain note explicitly cites 'PHP/Apache/Nginx worker processes spawning unusual children (sh, curl, wget)' as the execution-phase pivot. Pairing the parent web-tier binary with download/shell child binaries follows the BluRaven process-tree pattern and avoids the anti-bare-process-execution smell. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1505/003/
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1505.003 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • WordPress backup plugins (UpdraftPlus, Duplicator) spawning curl/wget to push backups to S3/Google Drive
  • cron-driven WordPress maintenance scripts launched via sudo from www-data running curl health checks
  • Composer/npm installs triggered by site management tools spawning python/perl for build steps
  • cPanel/Plesk panel actions running shell wrappers from the web tier
Suppression filter
| where not(ProcessCommandLine has_any ("wp-cron.php","updraftplus","duplicator-pro","backwpup","composer install")) and not(InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "backup-script")
Response runbook
1. Triage: pull the child process command line and SHA256; check the destination URL/IP the curl/wget reached out to against TI feeds; correlate with WAF logs to find the inbound HTTP request that immediately preceded the spawn. 2. Contain: kill the child process and any backgrounded children; isolate the WordPress host from the network if a payload was downloaded; snapshot disk for forensics. 3. Hunt: search DeviceFileEvents for new files written by the same parent in the prior 60 minutes (likely webshells in wp-content/uploads); pivot on the source IP to find other compromised hosts; check wp_users + wp_options for the 'diksimarina' IOC and any other anomalous admin accounts.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("php-fpm","php-fpm7.4","php-fpm8.0","php-fpm8.1","php-fpm8.2","httpd","apache2","nginx","w3wp.exe","php-cgi.exe","php.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","wget","curl","python","python3","perl","nc","ncat","socat","powershell.exe","cmd.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("php-fpm","httpd","apache2","nginx","w3wp.exe","php-cgi.exe","php.exe")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("sh","bash","dash","wget","curl","python","python3","perl","nc","ncat","socat","powershell.exe","cmd.exe","certutil.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine),
(SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("php-cgi.exe","php.exe","w3wp.exe","httpd.exe","nginx.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine),
(Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where Facility =~ "authpriv" or ProcessName has_any ("audit","auditd")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("php-fpm","apache2","nginx","httpd")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("/bin/sh","/bin/bash","/usr/bin/wget","/usr/bin/curl","/usr/bin/python","/usr/bin/perl","/usr/bin/nc")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostIP, ProcessName, SyslogMessage)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/php-fpm'
      - '/php-fpm7.4'
      - '/php-fpm8.0'
      - '/php-fpm8.1'
      - '/php-fpm8.2'
      - '/httpd'

      - '\certutil.exe'

| ImageFileName=/(\/sh|\/bash|\/dash|\/wget|\/curl|\/python3?|\/perl|\/nc|\/ncat|\/socat|\\cmd\.exe|\\powershell\.exe|\\certutil\.exe|\\bitsadmin\.exe)$/i

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"

| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",

         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]

OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc
