description: Detects the Bun JavaScript runtime spawned as a child of npm/node/yarn/pnpm — the loader pattern used by TeamPCP Mini Shai-Hulud worm (setup.mjs/execution.js) including @cap-js/openapi@1.4.1.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jpvj-wpmj-h7rv
  - https://www.wiz.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-supply-chain-sap-npm
  - https://socket.dev/blog/sap-cap-npm-packages-supply-chain-attack
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/04
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1059.007

logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\bun.exe'
      - '/bun'
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\npm.exe'
      - '\node.exe'
      - '\yarn.exe'
      - '\pnpm.exe'
      - '\npx.exe'

      - '/node'
      - '/yarn'
      - '/pnpm'
      - '/npx'

    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'setup.mjs'
      - 'execution.js'

falsepositives:
  - Developers intentionally using Bun as a build accelerator in monorepos
  - CI runners that invoke Bun from a node-based orchestrator
level: high
source:windows.sysmon AND @EventID:1 AND @Image:(*\bun.exe OR *\Bun.exe OR *\BUN.EXE OR */bun) AND (@ParentImage:(*\npm.exe OR *\NPM.EXE OR *\node.exe OR *\Node.exe OR *\NODE.EXE OR *\yarn.exe OR *\pnpm.exe OR *\npx.exe OR */npm OR */node OR */yarn OR */pnpm OR */npx) OR @CommandLine:(*setup.mjs* OR *execution.js* OR *preinstall*) OR @ParentCommandLine:(*preinstall* OR *setup.mjs*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/[\\\/]bun(\.exe)?$/i | (ParentBaseFileName=/(npm|node|yarn|pnpm|npx)(\.exe|-cli\.js)?$/i OR CommandLine=/(setup\.mjs|execution\.js|preinstall)/i) | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, ParentBaseFileName, CommandLine], function=[count(), min(@timestamp), max(@timestamp)]) | sort(_count, order=desc)
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process values(Processes.process_path) as process_path values(Processes.parent_process) as parent_process from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("bun.exe","bun")) AND (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("npm.exe","npm-cli.js","node.exe","node","yarn.exe","yarn","pnpm.exe","pnpm","npx.exe","npx") OR Processes.parent_process="*preinstall*" OR Processes.parent_process="*setup.mjs*" OR Processes.process="*setup.mjs*" OR Processes.process="*execution.js*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process values(Processes.process_path) as process_path values(Processes.parent_process) as parent_process from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("bun.exe","bun")) AND (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("npm.exe","npm-cli.js","node.exe","node","yarn.exe","yarn","pnpm.exe","pnpm","npx.exe","npx") OR Processes.parent_process="*preinstall*" OR Processes.parent_process="*setup.mjs*" OR Processes.process="*setup.mjs*" OR Processes.process="*execution.js*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Mini Shai-Hulud payload SHA256 on disk (7c24b4d9...e627144e8b) AIInstallation Medium
Hash-based detection for the specific malicious payload binary tied to @cap-js/openapi@1.4.1 in GHSA-jpvj-wpmj-h7rv. Catches the file at write-time (DeviceFileEvents) and at any subsequent execution attempt — definitive identification with effectively zero FP risk. Rationale: Direct SHA256/SHA1 IOC pivots from the GHSA advisory itself. Hash-on-disk and hash-on-execution coverage closes both the install and the run pathway; multi-table union catches it whether the file lands during npm install, gets loaded as a DLL/module, or runs as a process. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jpvj-wpmj-h7rv • https://www.wiz.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-supply-chain-sap-npm
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Sample stored in a malware-analysis VM / sandbox
  • Forensic disk image of an affected workstation mounted for investigation
  • EDR / AV vendor signature database update containing the hash as a definition (file path will give it away)
  • Threat-intel-platform ingestion of the IOC into a flat-file IOC repo on a SOC analyst's box
Suppression filter
| where FolderPath !has_any (@"\Quarantine\", @"\Malware\", @"\Sandbox\", @"\IOC-store\", @"\samples\")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: confirm the file path (real victim files land under node_modules/@cap-js/openapi/... or a sibling Mini Shai-Hulud scope's node_modules; sandbox/quarantine paths are obvious). Identify the InitiatingProcess that wrote the file (should be npm/node/yarn/pnpm/bun for a real infection). Step 2 — Contain: kill the file's writer + any running process matching the hash, network-isolate the host, snapshot disk + memory. Revoke every credential that workstation could reach — assume harvest and exfil completed before detection (the payload runs within seconds of preinstall). Step 3 — Hunt: pivot the SHA256 across DeviceFileEvents / FileWritten enterprise-wide for the last 60d to scope all infected hosts, and across DeviceProcessEvents to find any cached install that has executed since.
// Mini Shai-Hulud payload hash IOCs from GHSA-jpvj-wpmj-h7rv
let badSha256 = dynamic(["7c24b4d9a8f448832f3752d7f67dcdbf1b7f0f41e10bf633efa175e627144e8b"]);
let badSha1 = dynamic(["d78c25443ec4a0d7f0a85776461f3b1163132537"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(DeviceFileEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(60d)
  | where SHA256 in (badSha256) or SHA1 in (badSha1)
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName,
            FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, SHA1,
            InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
            FileOriginUrl, FileOriginIP, Source="DeviceFileEvents"),
(DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(60d)
  | where SHA256 in (badSha256) or SHA1 in (badSha1) or InitiatingProcessSHA256 in (badSha256) or InitiatingProcessSHA1 in (badSha1)
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, SHA1,
            ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
            FileOriginUrl="", FileOriginIP="", Source="DeviceProcessEvents"),
(DeviceImageLoadEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(60d)
  | where SHA256 in (badSha256) or SHA1 in (badSha1)
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName,
            FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, SHA1,
            InitiatingProcessFileName=InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
            FileOriginUrl="", FileOriginIP="", Source="DeviceImageLoadEvents")
| order by Timestamp desc
// Mini Shai-Hulud payload hash IOCs (Sentinel)
let badSha256 = dynamic(["7c24b4d9a8f448832f3752d7f67dcdbf1b7f0f41e10bf633efa175e627144e8b"]);
let badSha1 = dynamic(["d78c25443ec4a0d7f0a85776461f3b1163132537"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(ImFileEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
  | where TargetFileSHA256 in (badSha256) or TargetFileSHA1 in (badSha1) or Hash in (badSha256) or Hash in (badSha1)
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, Account=ActorUsername,
            FileName=TargetFileName, FolderPath=TargetFilePath,
            SHA256=TargetFileSHA256, SHA1=TargetFileSHA1,
            Process=ActingProcessName, CommandLine=ActingProcessCommandLine, Source="ImFileEvent"),
(ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
  | where SHA256 in (badSha256) or SHA1 in (badSha1) or Hash in (badSha256) or Hash in (badSha1)
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, Account=ActorUsername,
            FileName=TargetProcessName, FolderPath=TargetProcessName,
            SHA256, SHA1, Process=TargetProcessName, CommandLine=TargetProcessCommandLine, Source="ImProcessCreate"),
(CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
  | where FileHash in (badSha256) or FileHash in (badSha1)
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer=SourceHostName, Account=SourceUserName,
            FileName, FolderPath=FilePath, SHA256=FileHash, SHA1=FileHash,
            Process=ProcessName, CommandLine=Message, Source="CommonSecurityLog")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Cloud/SSH/npm credential file access by Node or Bun during npm install AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts for the credential harvesting stage of Mini Shai-Hulud: Node or Bun (when spawned within an npm install context) reading developer secret stores — ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.npmrc, ~/.ssh/id_*, gh hosts.yml, kubeconfig, .docker/config.json, Vault tokens. These files are read by the malware to enumerate cloud/CI credentials before exfil. Rationale: Wiz, Snyk, Socket and Unit42 all enumerate the same harvest target set (AWS/Azure/GCP/Kubernetes/GitHub/npm/SSH/Vault). Detecting node or bun in install-context fanning out across ≥3 of these distinct cred file types within a single process group is the highest-signal behavioural pivot the malware leaves before exfiltrating to t.m-kosche.com. Anti-pattern-aware: threshold and process gate suppress benign single-file reads (npm reads ~/.npmrc every install on its own). Cross-checked against: • https://www.wiz.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-supply-chain-sap-npm • https://snyk.io/blog/mini-shai-hulud-antv-npm-supply-chain-attack/ • https://socket.dev/blog/sap-cap-npm-packages-supply-chain-attack • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/monitoring-npm-supply-chain-attacks/
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1552.004 T1528
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • AWS CDK / Pulumi / Serverless framework legitimately reading ~/.aws/credentials during deploy
  • GitHub CLI extension or git-credential-manager being invoked from a node-based pre-commit hook
  • Developer running `npm run deploy` that touches kube + docker + aws creds in sequence
  • Test harness that reads .npmrc, kubeconfig and .docker/config.json to validate dev environment setup
  • Node-based dotfile manager / chezmoi-style tool legitimately enumerating dotfiles
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("aws-cdk","@aws-cdk","pulumi","serverless","@serverless","sst","chezmoi","git-credential-manager") and PathsTouched !has_any ("setup.mjs","execution.js"))
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: pull the full set of paths touched within the InitiatingProcessId window — true positives almost always span >3 distinct cred ecosystems (AWS+SSH+npm+GitHub), legitimate tools usually touch one. Correlate the host against UC1 (t.m-kosche.com egress) and UC2 (bun spawned by npm) — any two of three confirms incident. Step 2 — Contain: revoke EVERY credential matching the touched files (rotate AWS keys, regenerate SSH keypairs, revoke GitHub PAT + npm token, regenerate kubeconfigs). Isolate host, snapshot, do not wipe — preserve evidence of what was harvested. Step 3 — Hunt: enumerate the developer's recent npm installs (npm-debug.log, ~/.npm/_logs) to identify the entry-point package; cross-reference to the Mini Shai-Hulud package list and notify any downstream consumers if the developer published packages of their own in the last 14 days.
// Mini Shai-Hulud credential harvest: node/bun touching multiple secret stores during install
let credPaths = dynamic([
  @"\.aws\credentials", @"/.aws/credentials",
  @"\.aws\config", @"/.aws/config",
  @"\.npmrc", @"/.npmrc",
  @"\.ssh\id_", @"/.ssh/id_",
  @"\.ssh\known_hosts", @"/.ssh/known_hosts",
  @"\.config\gh\hosts.yml", @"/.config/gh/hosts.yml",
  @"\.kube\config", @"/.kube/config",
  @"\.docker\config.json", @"/.docker/config.json",
  @".vault-token",
  @"\AppData\Roaming\gcloud\credentials.db", @"/.config/gcloud/credentials.db",
  @"\.azure\msal_token_cache", @"/.azure/msal_token_cache"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileOpenInfo","FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node","bun.exe","bun","npm.exe","npm","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("install","preinstall","setup.mjs","execution.js","npm ci","npm i ")
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","npx.exe")
| where FolderPath has_any (credPaths) or FileName has_any (credPaths)
| summarize HitCount = count(), PathsTouched = make_set(FolderPath, 50), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp)
  by DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| where HitCount >= 3
| order by LastSeen desc
// Mini Shai-Hulud credential harvest via ASIM file events
let credPaths = dynamic([
  @"\.aws\credentials", @"/.aws/credentials",
  @"\.aws\config", @"/.aws/config",
  @"\.npmrc", @"/.npmrc",
  @"\.ssh\id_", @"/.ssh/id_",
  @"\.config\gh\hosts.yml", @"/.config/gh/hosts.yml",
  @"\.kube\config", @"/.kube/config",
  @"\.docker\config.json", @"/.docker/config.json",
  @".vault-token",
  @"/.config/gcloud/credentials.db",
  @"/.azure/msal_token_cache"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node","bun","npm","yarn","pnpm")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("install","preinstall","setup.mjs","execution.js")
| where TargetFilePath has_any (credPaths) or TargetFileName has_any (credPaths)
| summarize HitCount = count(), PathsTouched = make_set(TargetFilePath, 50), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
  by Computer=DvcHostname, Account=ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| where HitCount >= 3
| order by LastSeen desc
(source:windows.sysmon AND @EventID:11 AND @Image:(*\node.exe OR *\Node.exe OR *\NODE.EXE OR *\bun.exe OR *\Bun.exe OR *\BUN.EXE) AND @TargetFilename:(*\.aws\credentials* OR *\.aws\config* OR *\.npmrc* OR *\.ssh\id_* OR *\.config\gh\hosts.yml* OR *\.kube\config* OR *\.docker\config.json* OR *.vault-token* OR *\.azure\msal_token_cache*)) OR (source:linux.auditd AND @process.name:(node OR bun OR npm OR yarn OR pnpm) AND @file.path:(*/.aws/credentials* OR */.aws/config* OR */.npmrc* OR */.ssh/id_* OR */.config/gh/hosts.yml* OR */.kube/config* OR */.docker/config.json* OR */.vault-token* OR */.config/gcloud/credentials.db* OR */.azure/msal_token_cache*))
(#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo OR #event_simpleName=FileWritten) ContextImageFileName=/(node|bun|npm|yarn|pnpm)(\.exe)?$/i | TargetFileName=/(\\\.aws\\(credentials|config)|\/\.aws\/(credentials|config)|\\\.npmrc|\/\.npmrc|\\\.ssh\\id_|\/\.ssh\/id_|\\\.config\\gh\\hosts\.yml|\/\.config\/gh\/hosts\.yml|\\\.kube\\config|\/\.kube\/config|\\\.docker\\config\.json|\/\.docker\/config\.json|\.vault-token|\/\.config\/gcloud\/credentials\.db|\/\.azure\/msal_token_cache)/i | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, ContextProcessId], function=[count(field=TargetFileName, distinct=true, as=DistinctPaths), collect(TargetFileName)]) | DistinctPaths >= 3 | sort(DistinctPaths, order=desc)

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.file_path) as paths from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.process_name IN ("node.exe","node","bun.exe","bun","npm.exe","npm","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe") AND (Filesystem.file_path="*\\.aws\\credentials*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.aws/credentials*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.aws\\config*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.aws/config*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.npmrc*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.npmrc*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.ssh\\id_*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.ssh/id_*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.config\\gh\\hosts.yml*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/gh/hosts.yml*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.kube\\config*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.kube/config*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.docker\\config.json*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.docker/config.json*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*.vault-token*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*GITHUB_TOKEN*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*NPM_TOKEN*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where mvcount(paths) >= 3 | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium

      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes

      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("7c24b4d9a8f448832f3752d7f67dcdbf1b7f0f41e10bf633efa175e627144e8b", "d78c25443ec4a0d7f0a85776461f3b1163132537") or SHA1 in~ ("7c24b4d9a8f448832f3752d7f67dcdbf1b7f0f41e10bf633efa175e627144e8b", "d78c25443ec4a0d7f0a85776461f3b1163132537") or MD5 in~ ("7c24b4d9a8f448832f3752d7f67dcdbf1b7f0f41e10bf633efa175e627144e8b", "d78c25443ec4a0d7f0a85776461f3b1163132537")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("7c24b4d9a8f448832f3752d7f67dcdbf1b7f0f41e10bf633efa175e627144e8b", "d78c25443ec4a0d7f0a85776461f3b1163132537") or SHA1 in~ ("7c24b4d9a8f448832f3752d7f67dcdbf1b7f0f41e10bf633efa175e627144e8b", "d78c25443ec4a0d7f0a85776461f3b1163132537") or MD5 in~ ("7c24b4d9a8f448832f3752d7f67dcdbf1b7f0f41e10bf633efa175e627144e8b", "d78c25443ec4a0d7f0a85776461f3b1163132537")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["7c24b4d9a8f448832f3752d7f67dcdbf1b7f0f41e10bf633efa175e627144e8b", "d78c25443ec4a0d7f0a85776461f3b1163132537"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

AVideo YPTSocket plugin XSS injection via webSocketSelfURI/page_title query strings AIExploitation High
Hunts unauthenticated exploitation of GHSA-8whc-2wmv-ww35 in WWBN AVideo by detecting HTTP requests to the YPTSocket token endpoint or WebSocket upgrade carrying HTML/JS payloads in the webSocketSelfURI or page_title query parameters. The payload is then broadcast to any admin viewing a page that renders the YPTSocket debug panel. Rationale: Anchored on the exact endpoint path /plugin/YPTSocket/ and the two attacker-controlled parameters (webSocketSelfURI, page_title) named in functions.php:21-24 and MessageSQLiteV2.php:91/110, combined with URL-encoded and raw HTML/JS payload tokens (including the article's String.fromCharCode evasion). Cross-checked against the GHSA advisory text and the AVideo repo paths cited in the PoC. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8whc-2wmv-ww35 • https://github.com/WWBN/AVideo
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.007
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal QA/security teams pentesting the YPTSocket plugin (legitimate XSS test payloads)
  • Vulnerability scanners (Burp Suite, Nuclei, ZAP) probing AVideo with HTML/JS canary payloads
  • Bug-bounty researchers replaying the PoC against staging
  • Legitimate AVideo dashboards passing rich page titles that happen to contain '<' (rare — utf8_encode source values normally don't carry HTML)
Suppression filter
| where UserAgent !has_any ("Burp", "Nuclei", "ZAP", "sqlmap", "nikto") and SrcIp !in ("<internal_pentest_ranges>")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: pull all hits on /plugin/YPTSocket/getWebSocket.json.php and the WebSocket upgrade with these parameters in the last 48h; URL-decode the query string and identify the actual JS payload, source IP, and User-Agent. Confirm whether the AVideo instance has the YPTSocket plugin enabled and debugSocket=true (the vulnerable default). Step 2 — Contain: block the offending source IP at the WAF/edge, disable the YPTSocket plugin or set debugSocket=false until patched (upgrade composer:WWBN/AVideo above 29.0), and force-rotate admin session cookies and CSRF tokens for any admin who was logged in during the window. Step 3 — Hunt: review admin-context API calls (user/role mutations, password changes, plugin enable/disable, content edits) from admin session IDs that overlap with the broadcast window; pivot on AdminUser browser sessions to outbound exfil to attacker-controlled domains in DeviceNetworkEvents.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has "/plugin/YPTSocket/"
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("webSocketSelfURI=", "page_title=")
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("%3Cimg", "%3Cscript", "onerror%3D", "onload%3D", "%3Csvg", "javascript%3A", "String.fromCharCode", "%3Ciframe", "<img", "<script", "onerror=", "onload=")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
let SuspectTokens = dynamic(["%3Cimg","%3Cscript","onerror%3D","onload%3D","%3Csvg","javascript%3A","String.fromCharCode","%3Ciframe","<img","<script","onerror=","onload=","fromCharCode"]);

    | project TimeGenerated, Host=Computer, SrcIp=cIP, Method=csMethod, Uri=strcat(csUriStem,"?",csUriQuery), Status=scStatus, UserAgent=csUserAgent),
  (AppServiceHTTPLogs

Talos weekly prevalent malware SHA256 IOC sweep (Coinminer / Procpatcher / KMS activator) AIInstallation Medium
Hunts process executions and file writes matching the five SHA256 hashes Talos called out as the week's most prevalent malware in their 2026-06-04 newsletter telemetry roundup. Covers Win.Worm.Coinminer (VID001.exe), Win.Tool.Procpatcher (sample.exe), W32.C0AD494457-95 (f_000b97.html), and PUA.Win.Tool.Kmsactivator (AutoPico.exe). Rationale: Detection is grounded on the five SHA256 hashes Talos explicitly named in the 'Most prevalent malware files' block (VID001.exe Coinminer, sample.exe Procpatcher, f_000b97.html W32.C0AD494457-95, AutoPico.exe Kmsactivator, plus the fifth truncated entry). These are confirmed-bad per Talos detection names — file-reputation match is the highest-fidelity signal possible from this article. No external sources cross-checked: the IOC list is a weekly Talos telemetry snapshot from today's date with no second source yet published.
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1496 T1588.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security analysts intentionally detonating samples in a sandbox / malware-analysis VM (especially analysts retrieving Talos-flagged hashes for testing)
  • AutoPico.exe / KMS activator hash firing on unlicensed Windows installs (common in test/lab environments and unmanaged dev boxes)
  • f_000b97.html cached in browser cache directories from a benign visit — file write triggers without execution (review FolderPath for browser cache paths before escalating)
  • EDR vendor sample-collection / threat intel platforms (CrowdStrike, MDE attack surface reduction telemetry) pulling sample copies for analysis
  • Legitimate AV scanners writing the sample to quarantine — initiating process being the AV engine itself
Suppression filter
| where FolderPath !contains "\\Quarantine\\" and FolderPath !contains "\\Sandbox\\" and InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsMpEng.exe","CSFalconService.exe","SenseIR.exe","MpCmdRun.exe") and AccountName !in~ ("system","local service","network service") and AccountName !endswith "$"
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: pull the matching event's FolderPath, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, and AccountName. If folder is a known sandbox/quarantine path (e.g. C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows Defender\Quarantine, sandbox VM paths) or parent is an AV engine, downgrade. Confirm the Talos detection name from the case statement against the article's labelling. Step 2 — Contain: isolate the host via Defender Live Response / CrowdStrike RTR network containment. Kill the live process tree; quarantine the file. For Coinminer (VID001.exe) check for persistence via Run keys and scheduled tasks; for Procpatcher review which process was patched (often AV/EDR tampering). Step 3 — Hunt: pivot on InitiatingProcessParentFileName to find the delivery vector (browser download? email attachment? USB?). Sweep the rest of the fleet for the same SHA256 over 30 days and for the parent's hash. If KMS activator triggered, audit the host for other PUA / cracked software via DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory.

let ProcHits = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where SHA256 in (TalosMalwareHashes)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256,
              ParentFileName = InitiatingProcessFileName, ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              Source = "DeviceProcessEvents";
let FileHits = DeviceFileEvents

union ProcHits, FileHits

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user

    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
